title: GPU fleet capacity, cloud accounts, IaC & CI/CD runbook - 2026 guidelines
author: Asha Patel
summary: Canonical guide and runbook for Redwood Inference infrastructure engineering focusing on GPU fleet sizing, cloud accounts & networking, Terraform/IaC module patterns, CI/CD build pipelines, and operational runbooks.
scope: GPU fleet sizing and autoscaling; cloud account structure and VPC patterns; Terraform/IaC module conventions and release checklist; CI/CD for image and infra; operational runbooks for capacity incidents, node replacement, and upgrades.
owner_and_contacts: Primary author: Asha Patel (Infra Engineer). Owner team: engineering (infra). Pager: infra-oncall@redwood.example.com. Reviewers: Miguel Rodriguez (SRE), Samantha Lee (Platform).
slos_and_capacity_targets: Control-plane API: 95th < 120ms. Inference p99: Hosted < 450ms, Dedicated < 300ms. Maintain 20% spare GPU capacity during business hours, 40% off-peak. Reserve additional 10% for canaries/rollouts.
capacity_planning_cadence: Quarterly capacity review (owner: infra capacity team) with 1y lookback, model growth forecasts, reserved commitment planning. Monthly alert & trend review (SRE + infra). Weekly oncall capacity checks for dashboards and eviction trends.
capacity_model_metrics_to_monitor: Active GPUs by region (gpus.active); workqueue length (workqueue.length); average and p99 tokens/sec per model; spot/preempt rate; queue latency and request rejection rate; prefix cache hit ratio (cache.prefix_hit_rate).
terraform_iac_conventions: Repo layout: modules/ (single-purpose, versioned) and envs/<region>/<account>/ compositions. Module versioning: semantic tags (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Remote state per account/region (S3 backend + DynamoDB locks). Do not store secrets in state; use KMS and secrets manager integrations. Enforce tflint and terraform fmt in CI.
terraform_example_gpu_autoscaling: module "gpu_autoscaling" { source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-infra/terraform-modules.git//gpu-autoscaling-group?ref=v1.4.0" account_id = var.account_id gpu_instance_type = var.gpu_instance_type min_size = var.min_size max_size = var.max_size desired_capacity = var.desired_capacity spot_allocation_pct = var.spot_allocation_pct tags = merge(var.common_tags, { service = "inference-gpu" }) }
module_checklist_before_release: Document inputs/outputs and examples. Automated linting and fmt in CI. Unit/integration tests (terraform-compliance or kitchen-terraform). Backward-compatibility review and changelog entry.
ci_cd_and_build_overview: Separate pipelines for image build, terraform plan/apply, and runtime deployments. Terraform plans require infra-owner approval for production. Runtime deployments use canary + metric gates (latency, error rate) before full rollout.
ci_pipeline_steps: 1) Build image: run unit tests, static analysis, image scanning. 2) Push image to registry with digest pin. 3) Terraform plan in staging with mocked inputs. 4) Terraform apply in staging after approvals. 5) Deploy to staging and run smoke & perf tests. 6) Canary to production subset (10%) for 30 minutes and validate metrics. 7) Progressive full rollout.
sample_ci_terraform_plan_step: cd infra/envs/us-west-2/prod && terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-infra-state" -backend-config="prefix=us-west-2/prod" && terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars -out=plan.out && terraform show -json plan.out > plan.json
account_structure_recommendation: Recommended accounts: mgmt (org admin/shared services), prod-hosted (hosted API/control plane), prod-dedicated (dedicated GPU pools), sandbox/dev, security/ops (logging/SIEM).
vpc_design_principles: One VPC per account/region pair. Dedicated subnets per workload: control-plane, inference-gpu, management. Use Transit Gateway or transit VPC for cross-account connectivity. Apply least-privilege network ACLs and flow logging for critical subnets.
networking_table_example: Account: prod-hosted | VPC CIDR: 10.10.0.0/16 | Subnets: control-plane:10.10.1.0/24; inference:10.10.2.0/24 | Purpose: Hosted API + inference frontends. Account: prod-dedicated | VPC CIDR: 10.20.0.0/16 | Subnets: inference:10.20.1.0/24; management:10.20.2.0/24 | Purpose: Dedicated GPU pools and infra management.
cross_account_iam: Use principle of least privilege for cross-account roles. Prefer short-lived STS tokens via OIDC. Shared roles for CI/CD and fleet tooling must require MFA, use assume-role with external-id and be audited. Rotate and review trust policies quarterly.
runbook_capacity_shortage: Symptoms: sustained queue growth, rising rejection_rate, p95/p99 latency regressions. Triage: confirm via dashboards for workqueue.length and rejection_rate. Check region provisioning and spot eviction trends. Short-term mitigations: increase autoscaling max by 20% if capacity available; pivot traffic to alternate region or model fallback; evict non-critical batches and increase cache eviction aggressiveness. Long-term: open RFC for incremental capacity purchase and region expansion.
runbook_node_replacement: 1) Cordon node and mark unschedulable. 2) Drain pods with grace period, allow KV cache warmup elsewhere. 3) Recreate instance via IaC module ensuring pinned AMI and kernel drivers. 4) Post-provision validations: nvidia-smi check and run /opt/redwood/bin/gpu-smoke.sh. 5) Remove cordon and observe telemetry for 15 minutes.
runbook_upgrade_gpu_driver_and_runtime: Create canary node pool with new image/driver; run benchmark-suite. Deploy to 5% capacity and run smoke/perf tests for 60 minutes. If metrics within thresholds, proceed with rolling updates (maxUnavailable=5%). Rollback on p99 latency regression > 10% or error-rate increase > 1%.
runbook_checklist_pre_incident: Dashboards and alerts configured with pager rules and escalation. Playbook links embedded in alert descriptions. Quarterly game-day tests of runbooks and emergency procedures.
safety_and_rollback_patterns: Pin AMI/image digests in Terraform. Use traffic-shifting with automated metric gates. Maintain at least two compatible model variants per critical route for graceful degradation. Keep a warm standby region for rapid traffic pivot.
faqs: Q: When to request reserved (Dedicated) capacity vs hosted? A: Reserved for predictable sustained throughput, data isolation, or enterprise contracts. Hosted for bursty or low-commit workloads. Q: How conservative with spot allocation? A: Default spot <= 30% of prod capacity unless workload tolerates preemption and fast replacements are validated.
